a2-166.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Has the Key?
a2-166.scenario: Meg, Károly and Anna are about to leave the flat. Anna asks who has the umbrella and who has the key. You (Meg) have the umbrella, and Károly has the key.
a2-166.prompt: Tell Anna that you have the umbrella, and that Károly is the one who has the key.
cues: Say that you have the umbrella
Say that Károly has the key
a2-166.target: Az esernyő nálam van, a kulcs pedig nála.
a2-166.english: The umbrella is with me, and the key is with him.
a2-166.canDo: I can use adessive pronouns (nálam, nálad, nála...) to say who has an item right now.

a2-167.title: Communicative Challenge: Come Over to My Place
a2-167.scenario: You (Meg) want to invite Anna to your place on Saturday. Károly is coming too.
a2-167.prompt: Invite Anna to your place on Saturday and tell her that Károly is coming over as well.
cues: Invite her to your place on Saturday
Say that Károly is coming over too
a2-167.target: Gyere el hozzám szombaton! Károly is átjön hozzám.
a2-167.english: Come over to my place on Saturday! Károly is coming over to my place too.
a2-167.canDo: I can use allative personal pronouns (hozzám, hozzád, hozzá...) to invite people over.

a2-168.title: Communicative Challenge: Asking Péter for Help
a2-168.scenario: Meg is visiting Péter. She needs help with her homework and has no pen.
a2-168.prompt: Ask Péter whether you can ask him for help, and whether you can borrow a pen from him.
cues: Ask if you can ask him for help
Ask if you can borrow a pen from him
a2-168.target: Kérhetek tőled segítséget? Kölcsönkérhetek tőled egy tollat?
a2-168.english: Can I ask you for help? Can I borrow a pen from you?
a2-168.canDo: I can use ablative personal pronouns (tőlem, tőled, tőle...) with verbs of requesting, receiving, and departing.

a2-169.title: Communicative Challenge: What Did They Say About Me?
a2-169.scenario: Meg meets Péter for the first time. Péter says that Károly has told him a lot about her.
a2-169.prompt: Tell Péter that you have heard a lot about him as well, and ask what they said about you.
cues: Say you have also heard a lot about him
Ask what they said about you
a2-169.target: Én is sokat hallottam rólad. Mit mondtak rólam?
a2-169.english: I have heard a lot about you too. What did they say about me?
a2-169.canDo: I can use delative personal pronouns (rólam, rólad, róla...) to discuss people and topics.

a2-170.title: Communicative Challenge: Dinner at Károly's
a2-170.scenario: Károly and Péter have invited Meg and Anna for dinner. Meg arrives, and Károly welcomes her at the door.
a2-170.prompt: Thank Károly and Péter politely, and say that you always like going to their place.
cues: Thank them and say it is kind of them
Say that you always like going to their place
a2-170.target: Nagyon kedves tőletek, köszönöm! Mindig szívesen megyünk hozzátok.
a2-170.english: That is very kind of you, thank you! We always like going to your place.
a2-170.canDo: I can interact naturally as a guest or host using the proximity pronoun system.

a2-170-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Recipe Is at My Place
a2-170-consolidation.scenario: Anna wants to cook goulash but does not know the recipe. You (Meg) have the recipe at home.
a2-170-consolidation.prompt: Tell Anna that the recipe is at your place, invite her over tonight, say that she can ask you for help, and that you will tell her everything about it.
cues: Say she can ask you for help
Say you will tell her everything about it
a2-170-consolidation.target: A recept nálam van, gyere át hozzám ma este! Kérj tőlem segítséget, és mindent elmesélek róla.
a2-170-consolidation.english: The recipe is at my place, come over to my place tonight! Ask me for help, and I will tell you everything about it.
a2-170-consolidation.canDo: I can use the pronouns nál-, hozzá-, től- and ról- to say at, to, from and about a person.
